title: Improvement by a best local label
statement: Let $D$ be a finite nonempty label set, and let a constraint satisfaction instance on a variable set $V$ have a nonempty multiset of constraints in which every variable occurs. For any family of probability laws on $D$ and any variable $v$, replacing the law at $v$ by the point mass at a label maximizing the expected number of satisfied constraints involving $v$ does not decrease the instance's local expected value.
hypotheses_covered: Every declared variable occurs in some constraint scope
A probability law on labels for each variable
